items.title: Meet Chat: Our In-house Studio Assistant
items.excerpt: Suno details Chat, the AI assistant built into Suno Studio that can generate stems and plugins, rename tracks, move multiple faders, insert plugin chains across a session and suggest creative directions.
items.rationale: New feature, from the primary source. Producers working in Suno Studio can hand session chores to Chat (stems, fader moves, plugin chains across tracks) starting now.

items.title: 나이비, 하이엔드 음악 유통사 HREUM(흐름) 출범…AI 공동창작 음악도 듣고 판단해 유통
items.excerpt: Naibi launched HREUM, a curated distributor that accepts 'AI co-created' music made with tools like Suno, judging each track by listening before distribution.
items.rationale: A new distributor launch with an explicit policy: AI co-created tracks (e.g. made with Suno) are accepted and judged by ear rather than blanket-banned. Creators who use AI tools get a concrete distribution route while other channels tighten AI filters.

items.title: Alphabet shareholder sues Sundar Pichai and 12 others over training Google's AI, including Lyria, on copyrighted works
items.excerpt: Shareholder Phil Rosen filed a 79-page derivative suit on Oct 30 in Chicago federal court alleging Alphabet's leadership knowingly trained AI models, including the Lyria music models, on copyrighted recordings, compositions, lyrics and voices.
items.rationale: A new filing (Oct 30) of a new kind: a derivative suit that holds Google's leadership personally responsible for training Lyria on copyrighted music. It opens a legal front that the label suits against Suno have not touched.

items.title: Kid Rock Reveals He Used AI on New Song with Eminem
items.excerpt: Kid Rock says he used AI to create part of 'Heal My Faith', his Eminem collaboration on the Christian album Halfway 2 Jesus - reportedly the gospel choir - calling AI 'another tool'.
items.rationale: A major-artist release that openly uses AI for one element, reportedly the gospel choir. It is a concrete case of AI generating a session-player part on a mainstream record.

items.title: 일본음악저작권협회, 인간이 창작한 음악 보호 위해 AI 생성곡 탐지 나서
items.excerpt: JASRAC is excluding AI-generated songs from copyright management and pursuing a detection system to identify AI-made tracks, since registrations rely on composers' self-declaration (per Asahi Shimbun, Oct 30).
items.rationale: A new policy from Japan's largest collecting society: AI-generated songs are excluded from rights management and checked by a detection system, rather than relying on composers to declare AI use. Songwriters registering works in Japan are directly affected.
